steps.name: Sample structure QC on the 2-sample liver count matrix
caveats: Design has 1 sample per condition; standard multi-sample QC diagnostics (e.g., outlier detection by group clustering) do not apply
steps.context: Input: /eval-four-models-with-no-replicates-1v1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 2 sample columns + gene symbol column, raw integer salmon-derived counts) and /eval-four-models-with-no-replicates-1v1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (2 rows x 2 columns, one row per sample with condition: treated/control). Homo sapiens, liver tissue.
steps.question: Given the single treated and single control liver sample, what do library sizes, the variance-stabilized expression distribution, and the top-variable-gene profile show about basic sample quality and comparability, before any fold-change computation?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC (vst blind, top-variable-gene profile, sample distance) per R-0033@40bf, adapted since only 2 samples exist total

constraints: n_top_genes = 500, transform = vst(blind=TRUE) per grounded QC procedure
Do not attempt a PCA scatter plot claim across replicates — there are none; report only descriptive distance/variance metrics
acceptance_criteria: Reports total and per-sample library size (sum of raw counts) for both the treated and the control liver sample
Applies DESeq2 vst(blind=TRUE) to the count matrix after loading counts.csv and metadata.csv
Reports the top 500 most-variable genes by variance across the two vst-transformed samples and a sample-to-sample Euclidean distance/correlation
Explicitly states in output that with n=1 per group no PCA of within-group scatter is possible and this QC is descriptive only

steps.name: Descriptive log2 fold changes, treated vs control (no inferential test)
caveats: No biological replication in either arm: report is descriptive only, not evidence of statistically significant differential expression
A large descriptive fold change in a low-count gene can be noise; the report should flag genes with normalized counts near the filtering threshold
steps.context: Same input files as T1S1. This step must NOT run DESeq() Wald/LRT testing or report any p-value — the knowledge service's design-check rule (no replication in either group) forbids inferential DE testing here.
steps.question: Which genes differ in expression between the single treated liver sample and the single control liver sample, reported as descriptive, size-factor-normalized log2 fold changes since no biological replication exists to support a hypothesis test?

grounding.reason: R-0003@6b3a mandates descriptive-only output (no inferential test) because n=1 per group; R-0002/R-0026/R-0036 ground the filter, normalization, and explicit-reference-level choices

constraints: min_count = 10, min_samples = 1 (smallest group size) for the low-count filter
Normalization: DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, computed via estimateSizeFactors on the 2-sample matrix (not pre-scaled counts)
Reference/contrast: condition factor releveled so 'control' is the reference; report contrast as treated_vs_control
Do NOT call DESeq()'s significance testing, do NOT run apeglm/ashr shrinkage, and do NOT compute or report any p-value/FDR — these require a fitted dispersion this design cannot estimate

tximport is not available in this environment; the analysis reads the provided pre-summarized gene x sample count matrix directly via DESeqDataSetFromMatrix rather than through tximport-based import with length offsets — state this deviation in the output
acceptance_criteria: Filters out genes with fewer than 10 raw counts in at least 1 sample (smallest group size = 1) before computing fold changes
Computes DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors from the 2-sample count matrix and reports size-factor-normalized counts for both samples

Computes descriptive log2 fold change as log2((normalized_count_treated + pseudocount) / (normalized_count_control + pseudocount)) for every filtered gene, explicit reference level = control (denominator), treated = numerator
Produces a full ranked table (all tested genes) sorted by descriptive log2FC, with no p-value, no adjusted p-value, and no significance call reported anywhere in the output

Output explicitly states: 'No inferential differential expression test was performed; this design (1 treated, 1 control, no replicates) does not support dispersion estimation. Values below are descriptive fold changes only.'
Reports the count of genes tested after filtering (out of 12000 total) and the top 25 up- and top 25 down-ranked genes by descriptive log2FC

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on descriptive fold-change ranking (Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways)
caveats: The design flag (no replication) propagates into enrichment: any p-value fgsea reports reflects gene-permutation null variance, not biological replicate variance, so it is not a valid test of a treated-vs-control difference
Reactome GMT covers all species in one file; must be restricted to Homo sapiens via the paired index file before running fgsea
If fewer than ~50 genes would ordinarily be called significant, this reinforces using the ranked (fgsea) method rather than any over-representation test — no ORA is planned here

Gene symbols in counts.csv are HGNC-style; no explicit Entrez mapping needed if the sets are symbol-keyed (they are, per the store's contents descriptions), but report any unmapped symbols.

grounding.reason: fgsea preranked GSEA on Hallmark then Reactome/WikiPathways per R-0048/R-0165; flagged descriptive-only per R-0003@6b3a since the underlying ranking has no inferential basis

constraints: rank_metric = descriptive_log2_fold_change (stated choice, since no Wald/moderated-t statistic exists for this 1-vs-1 design)
min_size = 15, max_size = 500 (applied after intersecting each set with the tested gene universe)
universe = tested genes from T1S2's post-filter list, not the whole genome
Treat this enrichment step as descriptive per R-0003; do not present any set as a proven finding
acceptance_criteria: Uses the full ranked list of all genes tested in T1S2 (post-filter), ranked by descriptive log2 fold change (stated ranking metric, since no Wald statistic exists for this design)
Runs fgsea against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (50 sets) as the primary collection, applying a gene set size window of 15-500 members among the tested genes

Runs a follow-up fgsea pass against the Reactome human pathway gene sets and the WikiPathways human gene sets (filtered to Homo sapiens), each with the same size window, reported as separate tables not merged with Hallmark
Reports which fraction of the input gene symbols mapped/matched entries in each gene set collection
Collapses redundant/overlapping leading-edge gene sets and reports one representative per redundant group, keeping the full table as supplement

States explicitly that fgsea's normalized enrichment score and nominal/adjusted p-value are reported for reference only and are NOT valid inferential evidence given the underlying descriptive (non-tested) gene ranking; leading-edge genes are reported for every top-ranked set regardless of the p-value
Reports the gene set collection version/release used for Hallmark (2026.1), Reactome (current), and WikiPathways (2026.07.10 human)

plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE, no replicates
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile is a raw salmon-derived gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 3 columns incl. gene symbol -> 2 samples) with a metadata table declaring exactly 1 treated and 1 control liver sample and no biological replication. The knowledge service flags this design explicitly (rule R-0003): with one sample per group no within-group variance and hence no dispersion can be estimated, so an inferential DESeq2/edgeR Wald or LRT test would report p-values with no statistical basis. The plan therefore runs (1) sample-structure QC on variance-stabilized counts, (2) a DESeq2-based descriptive pipeline that filters low-count genes, computes size-factor-normalized counts, and reports ranked, descriptive log2 fold changes (treated vs control) WITHOUT any p-value or FDR step, (3) a preranked fgsea enrichment on that descriptive log2FC ranking against MSigDB Hallmark (with Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, all present in the reference store for human) reported as descriptive only (no enrichment p-value treated as inferential evidence, per the same no-replication flag), and (4) a final report that states the design limitation up front, gives normalized counts and the top up/down descriptive fold-change genes, and lists the reproducibility record (package versions, thresholds, gene set collection versions). No shrinkage (apeglm) or multiple-testing step is included because those require a fitted dispersion/test that this design cannot support (dropped per the knowledge service's full_plan answer). tximport is not installed in this environment, so the pre-summarized gene-level count matrix is read directly with a plain count-matrix DESeqDataSet path rather than via tximport re-import; this is noted as a deviation from the tximport-with-length-offset recommendation, since only the gene x sample count matrix (no transcript-level or length information) was supplied.
